chunks: And al-Naraqi said in Shu'ab al-Maqal:

Sheikh al-Ta'ifa and their leader and their teacher — he possesses illustrious noble virtues, overflowing glories, and manifold excellences… He was the most trustworthy of the people of his era and the most learned among them; the leadership of the Imamiyya devolved upon him in his time.

key_terms.أَوْثَقَ: most trustworthy, most reliable; a technical term of rijal evaluation
key_terms.الطَّائِفَةِ: the [Shia] community/sect; in this title it designates the Imami Shia

ai.seo_question: What did al-Naraqi say in Shu'ab al-Maqal about Sheikh al-Tusi's scholarly rank and leadership of the Imami community?
ai.summary: Al-Naraqi, in his rijal work Shu'ab al-Maqal, bestows the highest praise upon Sheikh al-Ta'ifa (Sheikh al-Tusi, d. 460 AH), describing him as possessing illustrious noble virtues, overflowing glories, and manifold excellences. He declares him the most trustworthy and most learned person of his era, affirming that the leadership of the Imami Shia community devolved entirely upon him in his time.
